name: Medovik
origin: A Russian honey cake, said to have been created for the wife of Tsar Alexander I, who disliked the smell of honey until it was disguised in this many-layered cake; thin honey-butter layers stacked with a sour-cream filling.

ingredients.note: sugar fraction of honey at 60% of flour mass, split by USDA honey composition as in castella.json

the classic technique whisks bicarbonate into the hot honey-butter mixture, where it reacts with honey's own mild acidity and browns further from the heat, rather than reacting at proof/bake temperature as in a Western butter cake

process.name: melt honey and butter
process.description: melt honey, sugar and butter together, then whisk in the bicarbonate off the heat

process.name: mix in eggs and flour
process.description: cool slightly, then whisk in eggs and fold in flour

process.name: roll and bake thin layers
process.description: roll into several thin discs and bake each separately

notes: Honey's real composition (USDA FoodData Central, as cited in castella.json) is split into its own sugar and liquid lines. Effective hydration is kept comfortably above the 0.6x-sugar dissolution floor by including a small milk addition alongside honey's own water, a modest, explicitly-noted adjustment for margin rather than an attempt to hit an exact published figure. The sour-cream filling between layers is a separately-prepared component, out of scope for this batter's formulation.
